title: Canonical completed coefficient pullback comparison respects finite quotient projections
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient data $p,a,q,k_0,k$, $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $\mathcal O_E$, $\varpi_E$ and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ ($n\ge1$) [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_{T,n}=(A_n)_T$ and $R_T=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}=\varprojlim_nB_{T,n}$ for $T=X,Y$, with projections $\pi_{n,T}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the inverse image and ring isomorphisms $c_n:g^{-1}B_{Y,n}\to B_{X,n}$ and $c_R:g^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], where $\pi_{n,X}c_R=c_ng^{-1}(\pi_{n,Y})$.

Let $P_g=Lg^*$ be the completed integral pullback [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Let $\kappa_{R_Y}:g^{-1}R_Y\to P_gR_Y$ be the specified map [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b). Let $\lambda_R:P_gR_Y\to g^{-1}R_Y$ be the CANONICAL multiplication/completeness comparison of [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback]: on a flat-term K-flat model [def-pc-kflat-complex] it is induced on the entire strict quotient cone by the finite maps $x\otimes b\mapsto c_n^{-1}(b)x$, the inverse-image comparison for that cone, and the inverse of the canonical completeness map. At finite level let $\lambda_n:Lg_n^*B_{Y,n}\to g^{-1}B_{Y,n}$ be $x\otimes b\mapsto c_n^{-1}(b)x$; its inverse is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. The coefficient sheaf $R_Y$ and its reductions are derived complete constructible coefficient objects [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible]. Let $\rho_n:P_gR_Y\to\operatorname{Res}_n Lg_n^*B_{Y,n}$ be the specified projection of the completed pullback model, using the canonical reduction $R_Y\otimes^L A_n\cong B_{Y,n}$ and restriction of scalars [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients].

Then the canonical comparison, including its actual cone maps, satisfies
$$\lambda_R\circ\kappa_{R_Y}=\mathrm{id}_{g^{-1}R_Y},\qquad \kappa_{R_Y}\circ\lambda_R=\mathrm{id}_{P_gR_Y},$$
$$\operatorname{Res}_n(\lambda_n)\circ\rho_n=g^{-1}(\pi_{n,Y})\circ\lambda_R,$$
and consequently, for $\theta_R=c_R\circ\lambda_R$,
$$\pi_{n,X}\circ\theta_R=\operatorname{Res}_n(c_n\circ\lambda_n)\circ\rho_n.$$
The equalities are compatible with the specified maps $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ before passing to the derived inverse limit. When $X=Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ for a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$ and $g=g_Y$, this is the canonical $\lambda$ and $\theta_{\mathcal O_E}$ used in [def-weil-constant-weil-structure](3), not an arbitrary isomorphism $P_gR_Y\cong g^{-1}R_Y$. This is a statement about coefficient pullback and its reduction projections, without a claim about Frobenius on cohomology.
